subject: Incident runway synthesis & QBR deck input
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Clarke <emma@acme-analytics.com>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident runway synthesis & QBR deck input

Team / Emma,

Quick recap and asks as we prep QBR slides this week. On Saturday 2027-05-15 at ~03:40 UTC we observed a cache invalidation bug that caused elevated P99 latency for the hosted text-generation path used by Acme's production environment. Impact window was ~12 minutes; we missed our 99.9% latency SLO for 7 minutes of that window. Customer-facing symptoms were elevated response times and a handful of 429s for long-tail requests.

What we have so far (attach: ACME_postmortem_v1.pdf):
- Root cause: threshold-based cache evictions combined with a race in background TTL refresh.
- Contributing factors: recent autoscaler tweak (scale-down aggressiveness) + a regression in our KV cache lock path.
- Detection: internal latency alert fired; on-call routed to SRE and infra lead.
- Mitigation during incident: hotfix to TTL refresh + temporary conservative autoscaling profile.

Action items (owners):
1) Fix KV lock race + unit tests (Karthik) — target ship: 2027-05-21 EOD.
2) Autoscaler rollback and safety gate (Hannah) — target: 2027-05-18 morning.
3) Postmortem writeup and customer note (Marissa) — sending v1 now; final v1.1 by 2027-05-18.
4) SLA credit proposal and legal sign-off (Vivek) — propose for QBR.

Asks for leadership/QBR deck:
- Vivek: confirm SLA credit approach and range we should present to Acme (ballpark).
- Hannah/Karthik: one-liner impact & mitigation we can put on slide (2–3 bullets each).
- Emma (Acme): quick confirmation that the attached v1 captures impact accurately from your side; any customer-visible metrics you want us to highlight?

Attachments: ACME_postmortem_v1.pdf, INC-4721-telemetry-snapshot.csv.

I'll keep this thread as the single source for QBR input and executive summary.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Clarke <emma@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident runway synthesis & QBR deck input

Thanks Marissa — high level ok from me. Quick clarifications and commitments: 

- Root cause confirmation: I validated the lock contention trace in the shard logs (INC-4721). The race occurs when TTL refresh tries to rehydrate a key while the eviction routine marks it stale — reproducer added to the ticket.
- Impact line for slide: "KV lock race triggered transient cache misses, increasing P99 latency by ~850ms for a 12-minute window."
- Timing: I’ll push the fix and tests by EOD Friday (2027-05-21). If we need to accelerate to the 18th I can cut a hotfix branch but it’ll be less tested. Recommend we aim for 21st and keep the autoscaler safety in place.

Also: I added a short CI check to prevent the specific lock ordering; will ship as part of the fix.

-Karthik
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

From: Emma Clarke <emma@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 13:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident runway synthesis & QBR deck input

Marissa — thank you for the detailed note and the postmortem v1. A few datapoints from our side:

- We saw a spike in client retries at 03:42 UTC that correlates with your telemetry. Rough estimate: ~1.8% of requests retried within that 12-minute window.
- Business impact: our overnight ingestion job slowed down and we had to re-run 3 batches; not material for revenue but operationally painful.
- On SLA credits: procurement would expect a formal credit calculation and a timeline for remediation before internal execs accept the QBR narrative.

Asks back to Redwood: please include the credit calculation methodology in the next note (simple formula + example). We can then route internally.

Emma
Platform Ops, Acme Analytics

On Mon, May 17, 2027 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team / Emma,
> 
> Quick recap and asks as we prep QBR slides this week...

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Clarke <emma@acme-analytics.com>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident runway synthesis & QBR deck input

Appreciate the clear distillation, Marissa. A couple of exec-level notes and asks for the QBR slide we will present to Acme and internal leadership: 

1) SLA credit approach (proposal): offer a one-time credit equivalent to 5% of May bill for the affected product path, contingent on the fix timeline (targeted ship 2027-05-21). Rationale: proportional but not precedent-setting; we can adjust if Acme provides metrics that materially increase impact.
2) Commitments to include on slide: 
   - Short-term: autoscaler safety gate (Hannah) + customer-notified mitigation (Marissa) — complete.
   - Medium-term: KV lock race fix + CI guardrails (Karthik) — ship by 2027-05-21.
   - Long-term: telemetry improvements for earlier detection + synthetic coverage for tail latency (owner: Platform Reliability) — roadmap item.
3) Ask legal/finance to pre-clear the 5% credit so we can state it during the QBR; Marissa to coordinate.

Please add one bullet per owner (2 lines max) to the QBR slide draft. I’ve created a placeholder doc (link below). If we can lock wording by EOD Wednesday the deck build and rehearsals will be straightforward.

Vivek
VP, Customer & Product Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Clarke <emma@acme-analytics.com>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 14:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident runway synthesis & QBR deck input

All — finalizing slide content and locking owners. I updated the postmortem to v1.1 (attached) with additional telemetry snippets and the SLA credit calc example per Emma's ask. Summary for the QBR slide (two lines each):

- Hannah Schmitt: "Autoscaler safety gate rolled; reduced scale-down aggressiveness to prevent rapid eviction — deployed 05/17."
- Karthik Iyer: "KV lock race fix in progress; fix + CI guardrails targeted 05/21; hotfix branch available if required earlier."
- Marissa Cole: "Customer note sent; postmortem v1.1 attached; monitoring dashboards updated for tail-latency."
- Vivek Kulkarni: "Proposed one-time 5% credit for May; legal/finance looped for pre-approval."

Attachments: ACME_postmortem_v1.1.pdf, INC-4721-telemetry-snapshot.csv, qbr-slide-draft.pptx

Emma — please confirm receipt of v1.1 and whether the credit example is sufficient for your procurement team. If yes, we will list the credit on the QBR slide and move the conversation to contract fulfillment after the meeting.

Thanks everyone — I’ll upload the finalized QBR slide to the folder and notify the deck owner.

Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
